I am extremely disappointed with my experience using the Simply Guitar app.

I was using the app's tuner to tune the highest string on my guitar. The app repeatedly instructed me to continue tightening the string, and because I trusted the app's guidance, I followed those instructions. As a direct result, the string snapped.

This was the final string on my guitar, meaning my instrument is now completely unusable. I relied on your app to help me tune my guitar correctly, not to leave me with a guitar that I cannot play.

I expect you to investigate why the tuner continued telling me to tighten the string instead of recognizing that it was already at—or beyond—the correct pitch. This experience has caused unnecessary frustration and has left me having to pay to replace my strings.

I would like an explanation of what went wrong and to know what you are prepared to do to resolve this situation. I expect this complaint to be taken seriously.

I look forward to your prompt response. (Ps I tonally don’t recommend to beginners)

reviews.title: Shouldn’t have to pay to learn music
reviews.text:
SimplyGuitar markets itself as an easy, beginner-friendly way to learn guitar, but in practice it is heavily locked behind a paywall. While the app allows a brief introduction, nearly all meaningful lessons and progress require a subscription. This makes it impossible to actually learn without paying.

Some premium features are reasonable to charge for. Advanced lessons, extra tools, or personalized feedback make sense as paid options. However, SimplyGuitar goes far beyond that. The app gives users only one short free course, and the moment you begin practicing and making progress, you are forced to pay just to continue learning basic material. Cutting off learning mid-progress is not acceptable.

This is especially disappointing because there are kids and beginners who genuinely want to learn guitar but cannot afford a subscription. Music education should encourage curiosity and growth, not shut people out because they cannot pay. Locking core learning behind a paywall turns motivation into frustration and discourages new players from continuing at all.

Overall, the app feels less like a learning platform and more like a monetization system disguised as one. The constant push to subscribe comes across as greedy rather than supportive. SimplyGuitar could be a great app if it allowed real learning and consistent practice before forcing payment, but in its current state, it prioritizes profit over education.
